title: Friction and Gravity
seo_title: Primary 4 Basic Science and Technology: Friction and Gravity Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 4 Basic Science and Technology: You and Energy
standard_text: Friction is a force that opposes motion between surfaces; it can be useful or harmful and can be increased or reduced. Gravity pulls objects toward the centre of the Earth; weight is the force of gravity on an object. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 4, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): friction, reducing and increasing friction, gravity, weight and mass. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Gravity pulls everything toward the Earth.
body_html:
How to think about it

Friction acts between two surfaces that rub. Rough surfaces make more friction than smooth ones. Friction is useful when we walk or brake a bicycle, but it wears out shoes and tyres. Oil and wheels reduce friction.

Gravity pulls objects toward the Earth, so things fall when dropped. Weight is the pull of gravity on an object and is measured in newtons; mass is the amount of matter and is measured in kilograms.

Example

Why do tyres have grooves?

Grip the road

Answer: to increase friction

Example

Which is measured in newtons, mass or weight?

Weight is a force.

Answer: weight

Common mistakes

  • Thinking friction is always bad.
  • Mixing up mass and weight.
  • Thinking heavy objects fall faster without air.

faq.q: Why is it easier to slide on a wet floor?
faq.a: Water reduces friction between your shoes and the floor.

faq.q: Would you weigh less on the Moon?
faq.a: Yes, because the Moon's gravity is weaker; your mass stays the same.

items.q: A toy car is pushed with the same force across four surfaces: a smooth plastic tray, carpet, gravel, ice. On which will it stop soonest?
items.e: The roughest surface has the most friction, so the car stops soonest.

items.q: A toy car is pushed with the same force across four surfaces: a smooth plastic tray, grass, gravel, ice. On which will it travel furthest?
items.e: The smoothest surface has the least friction, so the car goes furthest.
